headline: Calendars are shared only inside the organisation today; guests see free/busy through emailed invites, and the sharing model, the permission service and the invite flow are the three places this design has to change.
summary: Sharing is per calendar and per member, enforced by the permission service on every read. Guests have no identity: an invite carries a signed link that expires with the event. Two teams already export free/busy to outside tools by hand. The mobile client caches calendars for a week, so a revoked share can stay visible offline. No audit log records who viewed a shared calendar, and support has asked for one.

decisions.decision: Guests get a signed link, never an account of their own
decisions.rationale: The invite flow already signs links. Accounts would need a second identity store.

decisions.decision: Free/busy is the default share; event details need an explicit grant
A share can be revoked by the calendar owner and by an organisation admin
The week-long mobile cache stays; a revoke is enforced on the next sync
Viewing a shared calendar is written to a new audit log

risks.risk: Sharing is per member today, so a guest link scoped to a whole team calendar has no permission row to check against and may need a new kind of grant in the permission service
risks.change: scope the first release to single-member calendars

risks.risk: The mobile cache keeps a revoked share visible for up to a week offline, so a guest removed from a project can still read its schedule on a phone until the next sync runs
risks.change: shorten the cache for shared calendars to one day
